title: Fix root-level ordinal TV show naming
summary: Root-level TV filenames with embedded ordinal season markers now extract the show title from the filename before falling back to the source folder name.
reason: Live Re Zero files under the configured TV source root planned and published as TV\Season 04\TV - S04E## because the ordinal-season parser kept the root folder fallback show name.
behavior_before: A file such as [Erai-raws] Re Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu 4th Season - 01 [...] under the TV source root parsed season/episode correctly but used ShowName=TV, producing TV\Season 04\TV - S04E01.mkv.
behavior_after: The same filename parses ShowName=Re Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu, Season=4, Episode=1, and plans TV\Re Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu\Season 04\Re Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu - S04E01.mkv.
tests_added: ops/pipeline/tests/Unit/Invoke-NamingSupportChecks.ps1 adds a root-level Re Zero ordinal-season regression case.
manual_validation: Read-only live shared-file parser plan for Re Zero S04E01 - passed
targeted naming support check and live read-only parser plan - passed
rollback_plan: Revert the tv_parsing.ps1 helper/use-site and the naming support regression test; future root-level ordinal-season TV files would again require folder placement or manual rename/override to avoid TV\TV output paths.
notes:
Extract show titles from root-level TV filenames with ordinal season markers before using folder fallback.
Expose the new TV ordinal-season parser helper in the naming module function list.
Add Re Zero root-level ordinal-season regression coverage for TV output folder naming.

No Python runtime impact; this is a PowerShell naming parser and focused PowerShell test change.
